chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Salih, who linked it up through a chain of narrators, saying:
There are four things a little of which is a lot: fire, a little of which is a lot; sleep, a little of which is a lot; disease, a little of which is a lot; and animosity, a little of which is a lot.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things in which a little is considered a lot according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these four elements as 'multipliers' where a small quantity yields significant impact, a concept rooted in both physical observation and spiritual ethics. In Shia tradition, this serves as a warning against underestimating minor sins or ailments, as they can escalate into major consequences if left unchecked. The hadith emphasizes proactive moderation, particularly regarding animosity, which can grow from a slight grievance into deep-seated enmity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-84 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Salih who linked it up through a chain of narrators to the Divine Leader, “
There are four things a little of which is a lot: fire, sleep, disease and animosity.”
